title: Chinese memory maker CXMT posts blistering 466% leap in Shanghai IPO bulk of spending to be focused on DRAM production, no HBM in sight
summary: CXMT, a Chinese memory maker, saw a 466% surge in its Shanghai IPO. The prospectus allocated 29.5 billion yuan across three projects, with a focus on DRAM production. No HBM plans were mentioned in the prospectus.
insight: Chinese memory market expansion gains momentum with CXMT's massive IPO

title: Physicists turn particles in chaotic orbits into liquid computers but this fluid hardware still trails memristor rivals
summary: Physicists have created liquid computers using silica spheres in a water-lutidine mixture, but they trail memristor rivals. Each oscillator is a silica sphere of 3 m radius, capped on one side with 80nm of carbon and suspended in the mixture at 28 C. This novel approach to computing uses chaotic particle orbits.
insight: Chaotic particle orbits enable novel, adaptive computing architectures.

title: Open-source 3D-printed portable MRI machine built for under $70,000 DIY medical equipment costs less than 7% of a full-sized MRI machine s $1.1 million starting price
summary: The open-source 3D-printed portable MRI machine costs less than 7% of a full-sized MRI machine, offering a more affordable alternative for medical imaging.
insight: Access to affordable MRI technology can transform healthcare globally instantly

title: Minecraft system requirements raised for the first time in 17 years Microsoft now recommends 16GB of RAM and a 2020s or newer CPU to run the Java Edition
summary: Microsoft raises Minecraft's system requirements after 17 years, recommending 16GB RAM and a 2020s or newer CPU.

title: HP OmniBook X Flip 14 Review: Premium design, middling performance
summary: The HP OmniBook X Flip 14 offers premium design and features but falls short in performance value, making it less competitive compared to rivals.
insight: Performance lags behind rivals in the same price category.

title: 3D-printed F-14 Tomcat uses an FPGA recreation of the world s first microprocessor' CADC s MP944 chip controls the fighter s swing-wing system, among other things
summary: An FPGA recreation of the F-14 Tomcat's CADC has been successfully implemented in a scale 3D printed model aircraft, showcasing advancements in embedded systems technology. This project leverages Field-Programmable Gate Arrays (FPGAs) to mimic the original Central Air Data Computer (CADC) used in the iconic fighter jet. The recreated CADC controls the aircraft's swing-wing system and other vital functions.
insight: Reviving vintage tech with modern FPGA advancements unlocks innovation potential.

title: Zeiss expands German site that caps ASML's EUV scanner output first new building opens four years after Oberkochen site groundbreaking
summary: Zeiss Semiconductor Manufacturing Technology is expanding its Oberkochen site in Germany, adding 25,000 square meters of production space. This expansion comes four years after the initial groundbreaking, with the first new building now open. The move is expected to improve production capabilities.
insight: Expansion enhances Zeiss's competitiveness in EUV scanner technology production.

title: Jetway SMC-ARK1 A Rockchip RK3588 SMARC 2.1 compliant system-on-module
summary: Jetway's SMC-ARK1 is a Rockchip RK3588-based SMARC 2.1 compliant system-on-module for embedded computing and edge AI applications, featuring up to 16GB of LPDDR4x memory and dual GbE connectivity.
insight: Accelerates edge AI and embedded computing through high-performance processing.

title: Open RC Spotter is an open-source ESP32 telemetry and data logger for RC cars and toys
summary: The Open RC Spotter is an open-source ESP32-based telemetry system for RC vehicles. It logs GPS position, acceleration, gyroscope, and other data to a microSD card and supports live telemetry over Wi-Fi and ESP-NOW. This compact platform is designed for RC cars and trucks.
insight: Real-time RC vehicle data logging and telemetry for performance analysis

title: Creality Pika review An affordable, portable 3D scanner with infrared and blue laser modes

insight: Affordable 3D scanning technology for makers and hobbyists becomes accessible.

title: Quantum sensors are: emerging commercially, expensive, need standards
summary: Quantum sensors offer greater stability in natural force measurements, but are expensive. They provide precise readings of forces like gravity, outperforming traditional methods. Their high cost is a major barrier to widespread adoption.
insight: Precise measurements require high-tech solutions with high price tags

title: Professor's invisible prompt trap catches 32 students cheating on their midterm with AI
